review.candidate_policy: The reviewer records the exact candidate commit and must not reuse a prior sign-off for a changed head.
review.external_signature: outstanding: an appointed independent reviewer must run the published scope against a recorded candidate and replace signoff SO-2 with a signed record (reviewer, date, signature reference). Project-authored tests do not substitute for that signature.

threats.surface: client listener: authentication and session admission
threats.description: An unauthenticated or brute-forcing peer reaches command dispatch, guesses credentials or consumes unauthenticated session capacity.
controls: --requirepass / --requirepass-file with a regular file and no group/other bits; inline secrets shorter than 16 bytes are refused
AUTH failure budget and per-source failure limiting
AUTH is required before any non-authentication command when a password or ACL file is configured
threats.residual_risk: An unconfigured process serves the implicit Redis no-password user, and unauthenticated-session admission is not capped (F-01 / R5).

threats.surface: multi-user authorization: ACL users, keys, channels, categories
threats.description: An authenticated user escalates to commands, keys or channels outside its grant, or an operator misconfigures the default user.
controls: Versioned allow/deny ACL matrix executed against both pinned references and the candidate
A file whose default user is off is rejected instead of silently permissive
ACL keyspace safety and category-selector audits
threats.residual_risk: Not full Redis ACL semantics (S2) and no per-user command or memory quota (R5).

threats.surface: transport: TLS listener, probe trust and SNI selection
threats.description: A network attacker downgrades, intercepts or impersonates the endpoint, or slips past certificate selection.
controls: TLS 1.3 only via the reviewed rustls stack, no plaintext or insecure fallback
Probe clients require an explicit CA bundle and verify chain plus DNS/IP identity before AUTH
One invalid SNI key rejects the whole configuration generation
threats.residual_risk: Certificate status (OCSP/CRL) checking and terminator anti-bypass attestation are absent (F-04 / S5).

threats.surface: protocol parsing: RESP frames, inline requests, pipelining
threats.description: A malformed or adversarial frame desynchronizes the parser, executes unintended commands or allocates unbounded buffers.
controls: Finite bulk (8 MiB) and frame (16 MiB) bounds with explicit errors
Seeded fragmentation, random-byte and pipeline-consumption properties
Boundary and error-dialect tests over the same limits
threats.residual_risk: No external fuzzing campaign and no sustained adversarial corpus in CI (V4).

threats.surface: request service: slow readers, blocked clients, queue growth
threats.description: A client that stops reading, or a fan-out workload, grows output queues and starves other clients.
controls: Bounded per-connection frames and a finite client count
Blocked-client accounting and CLIENT PAUSE interaction
Backpressure on output rather than unbounded buffering
threats.residual_risk: No configurable slow-client threshold, kill policy or fair share for large replies (F-03 / O6).

threats.surface: host resources: process memory and kernel OOM
threats.description: Keyspace, indexes, buffers and fragmentation exceed the budget and the kernel OOM-kills the process.
controls: Logical key/value payload budget with rejection and capacity reporting
RSS and cgroup v1/v2 current/limit observation with an explicit scope
Persistent WATCH-history byte cap
threats.residual_risk: Observation is not enforcement: no RSS/cgroup bound, headroom contract or tested OOM behavior (F-02 / O1).

threats.surface: persistence: journal frames, anchor file, offline archive
threats.description: An attacker or corruption event alters the journal, anchor or archive so recovery loads unauthenticated or truncated state.
controls: Optional CRC32/HMAC framing validated on replay
Rollback anchor recorded outside the journal
Offline rillcache-backup archive with verification and no live-path dependency
threats.residual_risk: HMAC is optional, and archive encryption at rest is an explicit exclusion (F-06).

threats.surface: audit custody: audit log, keyring, syslog delivery
threats.description: An attacker edits or forges audit records, or credentials leak through logs.
controls: HMAC-framed audit records with keyring rotation
Bounded redaction of credential-bearing diagnostics
Syslog delivery tests
threats.residual_risk: Custody depends on the operator's external syslog storage; the process cannot prevent deletion by a host-level attacker.

threats.description: A compromised or unexpected dependency, toolchain or upstream archive injects code into the release.
controls: Vendored, locked dependencies with pinned upstream archives re-validated on every use
No application-level unsafe Rust; only the reviewed rustls/Tokio/CPU-affinity exceptions and their required transitives
Pinned reference versions for every differential and benchmark comparison
threats.residual_risk: No SBOM, image signature, provenance attestation or reproducible-build comparison yet (L3 / L8).

threats.surface: absent subsystems: scripting, modules, cluster, replication
threats.description: A partially present sandbox or topology surface gives the illusion of support and is trusted with credentials or data.
controls: Absent commands return explicit unsupported errors rather than generic failures
The declared profile lists the exclusions, and the compile/test surface has no scripting or cluster path
Adding any such feature requires its own threat model before it is claimed secure
threats.residual_risk: Any future addition must not inherit this model (S10).

findings.title: Implicit no-password default user with unbounded unauthenticated sessions
findings.tracking: R5 admission limits for unauthenticated sessions
findings.detail: Without --requirepass or an ACL file the process serves the implicit no-password user, and no cap isolates unauthenticated session capacity.

findings.title: No enforced RSS/cgroup memory bound and no tested OOM behavior
findings.detail: maxmemory bounds key/value payload only; RSS and cgroup values are observational, so the kernel can still OOM-kill the process.

findings.title: No configurable slow-client threshold or kill policy
findings.detail: Backpressure and connection limits exist, but operators cannot set a stall threshold, kill a stalled client or reserve a fair share for large replies.

findings.title: No certificate status validation or terminator anti-bypass attestation
findings.detail: TLS 1.3 with chain and identity verification is enforced, but OCSP/CRL status and a terminator attestation that cannot be bypassed are absent.

findings.title: Audit records are HMAC-framed and rotate through a keyring
findings.detail: Forged or edited audit records fail verification, and rotation keeps old keys verifiable without weakening new records.

findings.title: Journal integrity without HMAC is CRC-detectable only; archive encryption at rest is excluded
findings.risk_note: Accepted for the draft profile: HMAC framing is optional and documented, archives are created by the operator-controlled offline tool, and encryption at rest is an explicit exclusion rather than a silent gap. Revisit before any release claim.
findings.detail: A party able to rewrite journal bytes can produce a CRC-consistent but semantically altered history when HMAC framing is not enabled.

findings.title: Inline (non-RESP) requests are accepted and must stay inside the frame contract
findings.detail: Inline requests are parsed with the same finite frame bound, and seeded random-inline properties assert no desynchronization or unbounded growth.

findings.title: Absent scripting/module/cluster surfaces fail closed with explicit errors
findings.detail: Unsupported commands return explicit errors from a documented list rather than partial behavior, so no unsandboxed execution path exists.

scope: penetration test cases listed in the scope
signoffs.blocking_note: No independent reviewer has been appointed. Everything the criterion names except the external signature exists in this repository; the signature must come from a party outside the project.
